summary: Riverside sprawls across 81.5 square miles at the foot of the Box Springs Mountains, and from the higher eastern neighborhoods the western sunsets light up the Santa Ana River basin in a way that seems improbable for an inland city — but the real surprise is the scale of its institutional economy: the University of California, Riverside, March Air Reserve Base, and a constellation of county government offices make this a genuine job center rather than a bedroom community for coastal metros, even though plenty of residents do grind west on the 91 toward Orange County or north on the 215 toward Ontario. At a median home price of $542,100 against a median household income of $88,575, the price-to-income ratio lands around 6.1 — stretched but not crushed by Southern California standards — and median rent at $1,812 keeps renting within reach of a broader income band. The climate is emphatic: 9.9 hours of daily sunshine and an average high near 78°F mean summers are genuinely hot and dry, while winter nights dip into the low 40s with startling clarity. Downtown, anchored by the Mission Inn — one of the most architecturally distinctive hotels in the western U.S. — has a walkable stretch of restaurants and coffee shops that gives the core a real pulse, but drive five minutes and you're in classic car-dependent suburbia with wide arterials separating residential tracts. Mount Rubidoux offers a short, popular trail with panoramic valley views, and the Santa Ana River Trail connects cyclists and runners to a regional corridor, so casual outdoor access exists without needing to leave the city. Riverside is a place with genuine civic weight — a county seat, a UC campus, a historic downtown — but one where the inland heat and freeway-era street grid constantly remind you that identity and convenience don't always overlap.
